model_result.answer_summary: X = IBr (iodine monobromide). Ozonolysis sentence forces k = 2 C=C bonds (k+1 = 3 products); the printed 181.0 g iodine per 100 g acid with one-I2-per-pi-bond addition gives M(RCOOH) = 253808/905 = 280.451 g/mol, singling out C18H32O2 (linoleic acid, M = 280.452) on the fatty-acid lattice; the 36.57% iodine mass fraction of the analogous X-adduct then requires a residual mass r = 126.904*(100/36.57 - 1) - 280.451/2 = 79.887 g/mol = bromine (79.904), unique among halogens by hundreds of measurement half-quanta and robust across the full half-quantum windows of both measured values; multivalent X = IR'_v variants need non-halogen residuals (39.94, 26.63, 15.98 for v = 2, 3, 5).
assumptions: Trusted general law: halogen addition across C=C consumes exactly one reagent molecule per pi bond (HalogenAddition structure, stoich = 1), applied both to I2 (iodine-value reaction) and to the 'similar way' reagent X.
Standard IUPAC atomic masses as supplied with the exam: I 126.904, Br 79.904, Cl 35.453, F 18.998, At 209.987, C 12.011, H 1.008, O 15.999 g/mol.
Reductive ozonolysis of an acyclic chain with k C=C bonds yields k+1 organic products (trusted general law), used to read k = 2 off the printed ozonolysis sentence.
Printed measured values carry the measurement-policy tolerance of half a last displayed quantum: 181.0 +/- 0.05 g, 36.57 +/- 0.005 %.

Previous-part dependency T5-A3 resolved by deriving the fatty-acid formula inline from the problem-only material (ozonolysis + iodine datum + monocarboxylic fatty-acid mass lattice), consistent with the problem-stated 5.3 fallback.
source_gaps: The problem never explicitly writes the 1:1 halogen-per-pi-bond stoichiometry or the ozonolysis k+1 product count; both are standard, trusted general laws encoded as plain definitions/structure data, not axioms.

X is constrained to iodine-containing halogen-adding reagents I R'_v by the printed iodine mass fraction of the adduct and the 'in similar way' clause; a hypothetical exotic X outside this class is not derivable from the problem inputs and is flagged as out of scope.
